html:
If you’re thinking about getting window tinting, whether for your car, home, or office, you’re probably focused on heat, glare, or privacy. But there’s something more important to consider: your health.

Australia has one of the highest levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation in the world. And while some window films might make things look cooler, that doesn’t mean they’re actually protecting you. Not all tints block UV effectively, and few can prove it. That’s where ARPANSA certification helps.

Tint a Car only use ARPANSA certified tint across our automotive and building film ranges. Because when it comes to protecting your skin, your comfort, and your peace of mind, we believe in proof, not promises.

Most People Choose Tinting for the Wrong Reason

Most people get their windows tinted to reduce glare, cut heat, or create privacy. And those are great reasons. But the real threat isn’t glare, it’s the invisible radiation that comes with it.

UV rays penetrate ordinary glass. That means you could be exposed while driving, working from a sunlit room, or relaxing on your sofa. Over time, that exposure increases your risk of premature ageing, eye damage, and skin cancer.

In fact, Australia has the highest skin cancer rates globally. And while sunscreen helps outdoors, most people don’t think to protect themselves inside their vehicle or home. Tinting can help, but only if scientifically proven to block UV effectively.

ARPANSA Certification Isn’t Just a Label

The Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency (ARPANSA) is the government’s authority on radiation safety. It doesn’t sell tint. It doesn’t endorse brands. It tests and certifies products to ensure they meet national UV protection standards.

When a window film is ARPANSA certified, it has passed the testing for UV rejection. This isn’t a claim made by the manufacturer, it’s independent verification. The certification tells you exactly how much UV the film blocks, based on laboratory-grade measurements.

What Certified Protection Really Means for You

ARPANSA certified tints block up to 99% of harmful UV rays. That translates into real benefits:

  • Reduced skin damage and lower risk of skin cancer
  • Less strain on your eyes during long drives or bright afternoons
  • Cooler interiors with reduced reliance on air conditioning
  • Furniture, flooring, and car upholstery that won’t fade prematurely

Whether you’re shielding your baby’s car seat, working in a sun-facing room, or preserving the look of your living room, certified tints offer a layer of invisible protection that makes a lasting difference.

Frequently Asked Questions

Isn’t all tint UV protective? Some is. But only certified film gives you proof. Without it, you can’t be sure what protection you’re getting.

Will I pay more for certified tint? Maybe slightly, but the difference is small, and the long-term benefits are significant. You’re investing in safety, not just comfort.

Can I see the certification? Absolutely. Every Tint a Car store can show you the ARPANSA documentation for our products. We believe in transparency.

Is certification mandatory? No, but it should be. In a country with this much sun, verified protection should be the standard, not the exception.

Your Safety Deserves More Than Assumptions

ARPANSA certification gives you protection, backed by science and verified by a government body. It’s one of the simplest ways to help safeguard your health, preserve your interiors, and stay comfortable all year round.
